report.summary: Chunk 3 of harness.py: arms aggregation, run_tier2 with LLM calls, baseline snapshot/write, and detailed comments on c_beats_a logic.
risks: _ask | medium | Exception handling too broad; catches all exceptions and returns empty string, potentially hiding bugs. | Add specific exception types or log the error.
run_tier2 | medium | B text is capped at cap_tokens*4 chars before token counting; tokens_B reflects truncated text, not full repo. | Ensure documentation clarifies this behavior.
run_tier2 | medium | Provider detection only checks Ollama; other providers are not supported. | If other providers are expected, add detection logic.
snapshot_baseline | low | Baseline snapshots only tasks without error or focus_withheld; tasks with errors become 'new' next run, which may be unexpected. | Document this behavior clearly.
todos: Review _ask to ensure it handles provider errors without silently returning empty string.
Verify that run_tier2's B truncation is correctly documented and matches expectations.
Check if baseline snapshot should include errored tasks with a placeholder recall value.

claims.text: Tie-inclusive on purpose: a strict '>' here silently counted a BM25 tie as an A win, contradicting the 'C>=A' column header (report.py) and this function's own docstring ('if C ties or beats A ... that is reported loudly, not smoothed over'). recall_A==1.0 on every current hand_reachable task makes a strict C win impossible, so with '>' the tie case -- dumb retrieval matching the product at equal cost, the commercially damning one -- was the ONLY case that could ever fire and it was being absorbed into 'no'.
claims.where: line ~610 (comment in dict literal for c_beats_a)
claims.why: The comment explains the change from '>' to '>=' for c_beats_a. The code shows 'c_beats_a': recall_c >= recall_a, which matches the comment's claim of tie-inclusive behavior.

claims.text: B's tokens were ALREADY measured with the real tokenizer before this change (count_tokens is exact whenever tiktoken is installed) -- that part was honest. What was NOT honest: B is capped at cap_tokens * 4 chars before being measured, so tokens_B silently reflected a TRUNCATED text, not the real whole-repo size. tokens_B_true (added here) is the untruncated whole-repo token count, so a truncated B can never be mistaken for the real baseline.
claims.why: The code uses cap_chars = cap_tokens * 4 to truncate B text, then count_tokens(ctx_b) for tokens_B. It also computes whole_true_tokens_cache[repo] from full untruncated text. The per_task dict includes 'tokens_B_true' from that cache. The claim is consistent with the code.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (run_tier1) have no recall to snapshot and are skipped here -- they simply get no baseline entry, which makes them a 'new task' (not silently a pass) the next time run_gate sees them resolve successfully. FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file) are skipped for the same reason: there is no recall key to snapshot, and re-baselining a fence-refused task would silently launder 'never measured' into 'passing'.
claims.why: The code filters tasks: 'for t in result["per_task"] if "error" not in t and not t.get("focus_withheld")'. This matches the claim that errored and focus_withheld tasks are skipped.

claims.text: Only a local Ollama HTTP endpoint is probed (free, no key, no egress). The probe is a 2s GET to /api/tags -- it does nothing unless Tier 2 is requested.
claims.why: The code does: urllib.request.urlopen(host + '/api/tags', timeout=2). It only checks Ollama. The timeout is 2 seconds. It only runs when called (Tier 2).

claims.text: Never call this from an automatic code path -- a baseline that updates itself is not a ratchet, it is a no-op.
claims.why: The claim about automatic code paths is a usage directive; the code itself does not prevent automatic calls. The function is public and could be called from anywhere. No guard is present in this chunk.

observations.what: The comment on c_beats_a explains a deliberate change from '>' to '>=' to handle ties correctly.
run_tier2 computes tokens_B from truncated text (capped at cap_tokens*4 chars) and also stores tokens_B_true from full text.
detect_provider only supports Ollama; other providers are not probed.
_ask catches all exceptions and returns empty string, potentially hiding errors.
snapshot_baseline filters out errored and focus_withheld tasks, as documented.
